item.title: US uses French supermarket cyberattacks to smear Chinese AI, fueling broader tech containment push: analyst
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 18:17:00
A woman browses frozen food at a supermarket in France. Photo: VCG US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's attempt to link recent cyberattacks on French supermarket refrigerators to a Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) model, without presenting publicly available technical evidence, has raised questions over Washington's politicization of cybersecurity issues and its broader efforts to discredit Chinese technology, a Chinese expert said on Friday. Speaking at the Heritage Foundation on Thursday, Bessent claimed that a Chinese AI model had been used in cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems at French supermarkets, Bloomberg reported. "I don't know who here saw the refrigerators and 150 grocery stores in France that got turned off," Bessent said. "That was a Chinese model." The US official also claimed that Chinese models "are dangerous because they don't have guardrails on" their versions of the AI tools, according to Bloomberg. Bessent's remarks, which offered no publicly available technical evidence linking the cyberattacks to Chinese AI, raise questions about the basis of the allegation, Hu Qimu, a professor at the Maritime Silk Road Institute of Huaqiao University, told the Global Times. Cybersecurity incidents are complex and should be examined through objective evidence and technical analysis, rather than being used to fuel politically driven accusations against Chinese technology, Hu said. Bessent's remarks came after French authorities on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of responsibility for the October cyberattacks on commercial refrigeration systems across France. French officials warned that there would be consequences for Iran, Reuters reported. The incident had already attracted attention in China before Bessent made his remarks. On October 28, China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) published an article titled "What caused supermarket fresh food to spoil overnight?" highlighting the attacks on French supermarkets as an example of growing cybersecurity threats to interconnected physical infrastructure. According to the ministry, hackers reportedly exploited remote management interfaces to launch cyberattacks against the refrigeration systems of hundreds of large supermarkets across France. They remotely activated the forced-defrost function on refrigeration equipment and set the temperature to 50 C, destroying large quantities of fresh and frozen food products and causing losses that could reach millions of euros. The MSS warned that cyberattacks are no longer confined to stealing data in the virtual world, but can directly target physical systems and cause tangible damage. It also advised using strong passwords for all accounts, minimizing the exposure of industrial control devices to external networks and promptly disabling unnecessary remote access functions. The US has frequently imposed restrictions on Chinese technology companies on national security grounds in recent years, Hu said. By linking a cybersecurity incident in Europe to Chinese AI, Washington could further reinforce the so-called China technology threat narrative and create another pretext for suppressing China's AI development, the expert noted. In contrast to Washington's approach of politicizing AI security issues and overstretching the concept of national security, China has consistently emphasized balancing AI development with security and actively participated in global AI safety governance. For example, China has put forward the Global AI Governance Action Plan in 2025, calling on all parties to take concrete and effective actions in advancing global AI development and governance based on the objectives and principles of promoting AI for good and in service of humanity, respecting national sovereignty, aligning with development goals, ensuring safety and controllability, upholding fairness and inclusiveness, and fostering open cooperation. In the face of common security challenges posed by AI, countries should strengthen communication and cooperation, jointly prevent the misuse of technology and promote the safe and healthy development of AI, said Hu.

item.title: China urges Belgium, Luxembourg to play constructive role in resolving China-EU trade differences
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 17:51:00
The Ministry of Commerce of China Photo: VCG China attaches great importance to the EU's introduction of trade protectionist measures and hopes that Belgium and Luxembourg will play constructive roles in urging the EU to work with China to properly resolve differences through the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism and promote the stable and sound development of China-EU economic and trade ties, an official from the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) said on Thursday, according to a statement from the MOFCOM on Friday. The remarks were made when Ling Ji, vice minister of commerce and deputy China international trade representative meeting with Filip Vanden Bulcke, Director-General for Geo-economics and Economic Diplomacy at Belgium's Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs and Henri Schumacher, Secretary General of Luxembourg's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs during the 23rd China-Belgium-Luxembourg joint committee on economic and trade cooperation in Brussels, Belgium, according to the official website of MOFCOM on Friday. Ling said that economic and trade cooperation between China and Belgium, and between China and Luxembourg, has made steady progress in recent years, with fruitful outcomes in aviation, port logistics, biomedicine, clean energy and other sectors. China stands ready to promote the development of such cooperation toward a more optimized structure and higher quality, while fostering new growth areas in trade in services, the digital economy and artificial intelligence. China is paying close attention to the EU's trade protectionist measures. It hopes Belgium and Luxembourg will play a constructive role in urging the EU to meet China to properly resolve differences through the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, and promote the stable and sound development of China-EU economic and trade ties, according to the MOFCOM's statement. Vanden Bulcke said that Belgium attaches great importance to economic and trade cooperation with China and stands ready to deepen cooperation in shipping and logistics, cross-border e-commerce, biotechnology, agri-food trade and automotive industrial chains. Belgium supports resolving differences between China and the EU through dialogue and looks forward to further progress and tangible outcomes from the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, the statement noted. Schumacher said that Luxembourg is pleased with the outcomes of its economic and trade cooperation with China and stands ready to work with China to promote the high-quality development of the Zhengzhou-Luxembourg "Air Silk Road." Luxembourg welcomes positive outcomes from the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, which would help foster a stable and predictable economic and trade environment between China and the EU, the statement said. On September 21, China Post launched an international cargo route linking Jiaxing in East China's Zhejiang Province, with Luxembourg. This brings the total number of international and regional routes opened by China Post to 40 and increases the frequency of its self-operated intercontinental flights to Europe to eight per week. Operated by B777F freighter aircraft, the route primarily serves key industries in Jiaxing and the broader Yangtze River Delta, including electronic information, high-end manufacturing, cross-border e-commerce, photovoltaics and auto parts. It is expected to handle more than 12,000 tons of import and export cargo annually, providing efficient logistics support for enterprises seeking to expand into European markets. Global Times

item.title: China strictly prohibits all forms of surrogacy, violations will face severe legal penalties: official
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 16:49:00
Photo: VCG China strictly prohibits all forms of surrogacy, and organizing surrogacy constitutes a criminal offense, violates ethical norms, and will be subject to severe legal penalties, National Health Commission spokesperson Yang Jinrui said on Friday. So-called "surrogacy agreements" are not protected by law, and those involved may also be held legally accountable, according to the spokesperson. Some localities in China have reported cases involving surrogacy or the alleged illegal use of assisted reproductive technologies. For example, CCTV News reported that health and public security authorities in Changsha, Central China's Hunan Province, raided two underground facilities illegally providing assisted reproductive services in the city's Yuelu district on October 29, detaining 21 people suspected of involvement in illegal surrogacy and seizing drugs and medical equipment. item.title: Jensen Huang just stepped down – and US media can't wait to imagine 'China always loses'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 15:07:00
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Photo: VCG Shortly after Jensen Huang stepped down from Nvidia, Bloomberg immediately published an article declaring China the "biggest loser." The article's logic is extremely bizarre: The technological edge held by Chinese AI companies relies on smuggling American chips and distilling American technology, and the departure of Huang, who served as a "loophole" in US chip restrictions against China and a staunch advocate for Silicon Valley's open-source model, would be "extinguishing already faint hopes for cooperation on that front" and leaving China "stranded on the other side." It seems Bloomberg had this article prepared well in advance, just waiting for Huang to step down so they could attach this label on China. Over the years, US media has frequently labeled China the "biggest loser" in various scenarios, from the US mortgage crisis and the US-Iran conflict, to the depreciation of the Japanese yen. Whenever something happens, there's always someone claiming that "China has lost again," a recurring trope that has led Chinese netizens to coin a term to mock this phenomenon: "China always loses." In reality, this narrative is consistently proven wrong time and again. It reduces the intricate web of international relations to a simple, zero-sum game of winners and losers, reflexively interpreting every event as a "loss for China." This approach serves to uphold a psychological sense of "American exceptionalism" while allowing the US to evade the reality of the profound crises it faces at home. Such repeatedly failed "predictions" have not only eroded the country's own analytical capacity but have also, over the years, misdirected US foreign policy, ultimately exacting a higher strategic cost for the US. This Bloomberg article, which claims that "China is the biggest loser," is a product of the anxiety felt by certain people in the US. Unable to face or accept the reality of China's independent industrial development, they have resorted to a form of self-delusion to deceive themselves, as if by simply concocting a "loser," the US could somehow be spared from its own losses. As observers of this entire situation, we would like to offer a well-intentioned reminder: Huang has repeatedly advocated for open source and openness precisely because, in the tech industry, openness means life, while closure spells death. If openness really depended on Huang alone and his departure closes off channels for technological cooperation, the US may face bigger problems ahead.

item.title: Danish business leaders, former diplomats see opportunities in China's 15th Five-Year Plan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 12:46:00
Panelists take part in a discussion during a dialogue on China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, Nov. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Zhichao/Xinhua) Danish business leaders and former diplomats have said that China's 15th Five-Year Plan could open up new opportunities for economic cooperation between Denmark and China in areas such as wind power, pharmaceuticals and green shipping. They made these remarks at panel discussions on China's latest five-year blueprint and the China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, on Wednesday. Former Danish Ambassador to China Friis Arne Petersen said the plan covered a wide range of industries where the two countries could work together if policy conditions allowed. Petersen said China's push to develop new quality productive forces, including through advances in artificial intelligence, could shape future cooperation in industry, agriculture, environmental protection and energy. He pointed to pharmaceuticals as an area where Danish companies could work with Chinese partners on research, manufacturing and sales. Ove Ullerup, a former Danish diplomat and chairman of the board of Asia House, an association which works to strengthen ties between Denmark and Asia, said China's green transition targets could open up new areas of cooperation with Denmark. He noted that the two countries established a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2008 and launched a joint green work program in 2023. Peter Dige Thagesen, head of geopolitics at the Confederation of Danish Industry, said Denmark's strengths in wind power, electricity and green technology align with China's priorities, and cooperation opportunities also exist in life sciences, food production and green shipping. Thagesen said a survey of the confederation's members showed that Danish companies wanted to maintain trade with China while reducing dependence in critical areas. Hans Henrik Pontoppidan, secretary-general of the Danish-Chinese Business Forum, said Danish companies should consider new ways to work with Chinese partners on research and development, particularly in health care. Chinese Ambassador to Denmark Wang Xuefeng said the five-year blueprint has highlighted advances in science and technology, the green transition and further opening up, which would create more opportunities for Denmark and other partners. The event was jointly organized by the Chinese Embassy in Denmark, the Danish-Chinese Business Forum and Asia House. Attendees listen to remarks during a dialogue on China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, Nov. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Zhichao/Xinhua)

item.title: Macao holds photo exhibition to mark 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 10:55:00
Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai addresses the opening ceremony of a photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth in Macao, south China, Nov. 12, 2026. A photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth opened in China's Macao SAR on Thursday. (Xinhua/Cheong Kam Ka) A photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth opened in China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on Thursday. The exhibition recounts the legendary life of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, with over 100 pieces of historical artifacts and photographs, audio recordings and documentaries. Addressing the opening ceremony, Macao SAR Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai noted that Macao shares a profound and special historical bond with Sun. Macao is where he began his mission to do good for the nation and the people, said Sam. Macao is also a cradle of Sun's revolutionary cause, a safe haven in times of crisis as well as a spiritual home where he cherished family affection, said Sam, adding that the best way to commemorate Sun is to carry forward his noble spirit and strive for national rejuvenation. One of the five chapters of the exhibition was dedicated to Sun's career beginning at Macao's Kiang Wu Hospital as a doctor known for seeing patients for free. Wong Kit Cheng, a nurse at the hospital and a member of the Legislative Assembly of the Macao SAR, told Xinhua that she views Sun as her role model and will continue to serve the public by pursuing the mission to cure. The photo exhibition will run through Nov. 27. The Macao SAR also scheduled other events including seminars, themed city tours and the issuance of commemorative stamps. item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 09:03:00
CHINA / SOCIETY Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen By Xinhua Published: Nov 13, 2026 09:03 AM
Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.

item.title: Does Taiwan really understand major signals from this commemorative event?: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 00:23:00
A view of the Taiwan Straits is seen from Xiamen port, in East China's Fujian Province. Photo: IC Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun Yat-sen. No matter how "Taiwan independence" separatist forces attempt to stir up trouble, historical legitimacy and the moral high ground will always remain firmly with those who steadfastly advance national reunification and national rejuvenation. On the morning of November 12, a gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. In his speech at the gathering, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Resolving the Taiwan question and achieving the complete reunification of the motherland are hurdles that must be overcome in the process of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. At this important historical juncture, this high-profile commemoration carries profound contemporary significance and clearly sends extremely important signals. Do all sectors of Taiwan society, especially the island's authorities, get it? For Taiwan, the first signal lies in the significance of commemorating Sun for national reunification. "The spirit of patriotism," "national complete reunification" and "national rejuvenation" stand as inviolable historical orthodoxy and the moral high ground. Sun is a revolutionary forefather revered across the Taiwan Straits. Throughout his life, he traveled far and wide, with "revitalize the Chinese nation" as his most resounding rallying cry, and national reunification as his deepest concern. With remarkable historical foresight, he stated categorically: "Unification is the hope of all Chinese nationals. If China can be unified, all Chinese will enjoy a happy life; if it cannot be unified, they will suffer." This observation profoundly reveals that national unification and the well-being of the entire nation are inextricably bound together. By contrast, the current Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities have engaged in political manipulation through "de-Sinicization" for the sake of partisan interests. While paying lip service to "freedom" and "democracy," they have, in practice, abandoned their historical roots and betrayed their own heritage. This is not only an outright desecration of the shared historical memory of people across the Taiwan Straits, but also a complete betrayal and insult to Sun's lifelong patriotic commitment. Beijing's solemn commemoration of Sun is a major blow against "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and a powerful rebuttal of their distorted view of history, setting the historical record straight. The second signal is to further clarify the mainland's policy stance on peaceful reunification and opposition to separatism under the evolving circumstances across the Taiwan Straits. "Compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits are all Chinese. We are one family bound by blood ties that run deeper than water. As long as family members talk things through calmly and consult each other when issues arise, there are no disputes or differences that cannot be resolved." The political differences between the two sides of the Taiwan Straits are a legacy of history. However, as long as both sides uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus and sit down for face-to-face communication, there is nothing that cannot be discussed when it comes to the interests, well-being and development opportunities of Taiwan compatriots. Compatriots on both sides of the Straits are one family. Why should they allow themselves to be swayed by the antagonism deliberately stirred up by "Taiwan independence" separatist forces? Why should they allow external forces to turn Taiwan into a pawn in geopolitical rivalry? All sectors in Taiwan should recognize, in particular, that the door to peaceful reunification remains wide open, channels for exchanges and consultations remain accessible, and the interests and sentiments of Taiwan compatriots are given full consideration. They must not allow the DPP authorities' political manipulation in pursuit of "independence" to block the path of cross-Straits communication, much less allow a handful of politicians to hold Taiwan society's future hostage. The dead-end path of "Taiwan independence" separatism has already been firmly blocked. If the DPP authorities persist in seeking "independence by relying on external forces or military means," dragging the residents of Taiwan onto their war chariot, they will inevitably face a harsh reckoning by history and the people. The third signal is that only by adopting a broader historical perspective and an open-minded outlook befitting our times can we see through the layers of confusion, grasp the profound meaning of the principle that "family members should talk things through calmly." In the speech, President Xi highlighted Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, called for emulating, inheriting and carrying forward his invaluable spirit, and called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Once we break free from the information cocoons and ideological prejudices created by "Taiwan independence" forces and examine the issue from the broader perspective of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the profound changes unseen in a century unfolding across the world, the logic becomes unmistakably clear. If humanity as a whole should work together to build a community with a shared future, there is even less reason for compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, bound by blood ties, to be artificially divided. The grand vision outlined by Sun in Fundamentals of National Reconstruction has not only become reality, but has also grown far richer and more expansive than he originally envisioned. History and reality have repeatedly demonstrated that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. No matter how "Taiwan independence" separatist forces attempt to stir up trouble, historical legitimacy and the moral high ground will always remain firmly with those who steadfastly advance national reunification and national rejuvenation. We sincerely hope that Taiwan compatriots will recognize the prevailing historical trend, distinguish right from wrong, and join their mainland compatriots in taking concrete action to shoulder the historic responsibility of achieving national reunification and national rejuvenation. The best way to honor Sun is to make the complete reunification of the motherland a reality!

item.title: GT Voice: AI jitters in US raise stakes in China for S.Korea chip firms
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 23:43:00
Production of semiconductor chip File photo: VCG South Korea's semiconductor exports are booming, but a new cloud is gathering over the industry - and it comes from the US. In a report published on Thursday, the Financial Times, under the headline "AI jitters erupt after Democrats threaten data center build-out," warned that the construction boom could be brought to a standstill following the Democrats' victories in the US midterm elections. The political headwinds facing US data centers could spill over into South Korea's semiconductor industry, at least in part. In January, The Korea Herald cited analysts as saying that most memory products shipped by South Korean companies to the US, including high bandwidth memory (HBM) and server DRAM, are used in artificial intelligence (AI) servers and data centers. This leaves South Korean memory chipmakers exposed to any slowdown in US data center development, which could put some of the demand underpinning their exports at risk. The US is an important market for South Korean semiconductors, even if it is not the largest. In July, Chosun Biz cited data from the Bank of Korea showing that the US ranked fourth among destinations for South Korean semiconductor exports in 2025, with shipments worth $19.02 billion, up from $13.626 billion three years earlier. Its share of South Korea's total semiconductor exports also edged up, from 9.6 percent to 10.3 percent. The question now is whether political resistance to data center construction in the US could put the brakes on the growth of its semiconductor demand - or even cause it to stall or decline. For South Korean chipmakers, this is a development that warrants close attention, as well as a clear assessment of what it could mean for their export prospects. Whatever the eventual impact on US semiconductor demand, the AI jitters unleashed by the midterm elections may be enough to prompt South Korean chipmakers to think ahead. If they seek to diversify their markets against the risk of slower growth in US demand, China is likely to be high on their lists. The Chinese mainland remained the largest destination for South Korean semiconductor exports in 2025, taking shipments worth $74.46 billion, or 40.3 percent of the total. This comes as South Korea presses ahead with plans to expand its semiconductor capacity. The Yonhap News Agency reported in September that the country plans to double its semiconductor production capacity within five years. Yet with the outlook for US AI investment becoming less certain, South Korean chipmakers may have to look increasingly to non-US markets to sustain their export growth, further increasing the importance of the Chinese market. If South Korean chipmakers turn increasingly to China, they could intensify competition and put greater pressure on Chinese domestic memory producers. But the picture is more complicated. Memory chip prices remain high, with some segments poised for further increases, pointing to the strength of underlying demand and the potential of the Chinese market. One factor that South Korean chipmakers should not underestimate is the rapid technological progress of China's memory producers. Once they overcome the remaining technical hurdles, China's extensive industrial supply chains and manufacturing capacity could allow them to scale up production quickly, turning technological advances into a formidable competitive advantage. For South Korean chipmakers to maintain or expand their presence in China, they will need to offer Chinese customers their most advanced products. Finding a way to overcome US restrictions that prevent advanced HBM exports to China is therefore essential to that effort. That task may become harder. The controversy surrounding Jensen Huang, who has resigned as Nvidia's CEO, has fueled fresh calls in Washington for tighter restrictions on China's access to advanced chips. But with semiconductors so vital to South Korea's economy, its chipmakers have every reason to press for greater room to sell their most advanced products in China. It is a market where competition is intensifying, but whose importance to South Korean suppliers is also growing. South Korea should assert its own economic interests.
